empty.title: No domains yet
empty.description: This service has no address yet, so nothing routes to it.

primaryMovedHint: $(PRIMARY_DOMAIN) and PORT follow it at the next deploy.

deleteDialog.title: Delete this domain?
deleteDialog.description: {{url}} stops routing to this service right away.

primaryDialog.title: Make this the main domain?
primaryDialog.description: {{host}} becomes the service's main address, used by Open and $(PRIMARY_DOMAIN).

dialog.httpsHint: Redirect HTTP to HTTPS and get a certificate for this address.
dialog.pathHint: Only this path and what is below it go to this service: /api never answers for /apix.
dialog.portHint: The port the app listens on inside its container.
dialog.destinationPathHint: Added in front of the path the app receives, when it isn't /.
dialog.middlewaresHint: Extra Traefik middlewares to run for this domain, by name, one per row.
dialog.resolverHint: Leave empty for the default resolver. Wildcards need one that can do DNS challenges.
dialog.wildcardHint: Also answer on every direct subdomain of this hostname. The bare hostname needs its own entry.
dialog.stripPathHint: The service receives the request without this path, so /api/users arrives as /users.
dialog.wildcardUnverified: HTTPS on a wildcard is not verified yet. It depends on your DNS-challenge resolver, and shows as working only once the proxy really holds the certificate.
dialog.middlewareHint: A Traefik middleware applied to this domain.
dialog.protocolHint: The protocol the app speaks behind the proxy.
dialog.hostHint: The name visitors type, such as shop.example.com.

errors.host: Enter a full hostname, such as app.example.com.
errors.path: A path starts with / and holds only URL path characters.
errors.destinationPath: A path starts with / and holds only URL path characters.
errors.resolver: Use letters, digits, dashes and underscores.
errors.resolverRequired: A wildcard certificate needs a named resolver that can do DNS challenges.
errors.middlewares: Each middleware needs a name, made of letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores, with an optional @provider.
errors.upstreamServerName: Use the name on the upstream's certificate, in letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores.
errors.upstreamCa: Paste one or more certificates in PEM format.
